title: Check yourself: when finally runs, and what replaces it

questions.stem: Per this page, in which of these situations does a `finally` block not run?

options.text: The thread running the try block is interrupted by another thread
options.says: The page says interrupting the thread does not skip finally.

options.text: The try block calls System.exit before it reaches its end
options.says: The page names the JVM exiting first, as with System.exit, as a case where finally does not run.

options.text: The catch block rethrows the exception it has just caught
options.says: The page says finally runs after try and catch whether an exception was thrown or caught.

questions.stem: Per this page, in Java 7 and later, what should close a resource such as a file reader?

options.text: A finally block that returns once it has closed the reader
options.says: The page says not to use return statements in finally blocks, and to prefer try-with-resources for resources.

options.text: A finally block that calls close after the try block
options.says: The page lists using finally for resources as a pitfall when try-with-resources is more appropriate.

options.text: A try-with-resources statement that declares the reader
options.says: The page says to prefer try-with-resources over finally blocks for resource management.
